qa_pairs.question: When do Fall 2026 classes begin, and when does the standard add/drop period end?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Fall 2026 classes begin on August 17. The standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28.

qa_pairs.question: What is the normal undergraduate credit load for a Fall or Spring term, and what is the maximum in Summer?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring, and no more than 9 credits in Summer.

qa_pairs.question: How much is undergraduate tuition per credit in 2026–2027, and how much is the student-services fee?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Undergraduate tuition for 2026–2027 is USD 420 per registered credit. The student-services fee is USD 180 in Fall and Spring and USD 90 in Summer.

qa_pairs.question: How much of tuition does the Northstar Merit Scholarship cover, and which charges does it not cover?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition. It does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees.

qa_pairs.question: What attendance level is expected in courses that record attendance, and may a syllabus set a lower threshold?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

contexts.text: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A course syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: A Fall 2026 student drops one course on September 1. What share of that course's tuition is reversed, and why does that rate apply on that date?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: 50% of that course's tuition is reversed. The 50% rate applies from the day after standard add/drop through the census date; in Fall 2026 standard add/drop ends at 17:00 on August 28 and the census date is September 4, so September 1 falls inside that window. A drop by the end of standard add/drop would have reversed 100% instead.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed.
the standard add/drop period ends at 17:00 on August 28. The census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: What approvals and payment does a late add require after standard add/drop ends, and is that fee refundable?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

contexts.text: A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.
The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: What happens to a tuition balance that is still unpaid after the grace period, and what does the resulting hold block?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines. An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance, but it does not remove the student from courses that were already confirmed.

contexts.text: A five-calendar-day grace period applies to the account balance, but it does not extend registration or scholarship deadlines.

An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance. It does not remove a student from courses that were already confirmed.

qa_pairs.question: Which conditions must a Merit Scholarship recipient meet to renew the award, and after which terms is renewal reviewed?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Renewal is assessed after each Fall and Spring term; Summer enrolment does not trigger a separate renewal review. To renew, the recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

contexts.text: Renewal is assessed after each Fall and Spring term; Summer enrolment does not trigger a separate renewal review.

To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

qa_pairs.question: A student thinks their final grade contains a calculation error. What step comes first, and what is the deadline for a formal grade appeal?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must then be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground, such as a calculation error. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.

contexts.text: The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination. Disagreement with academic judgement alone is not a permitted ground.
A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor.

qa_pairs.question: What must a student do to request a standard leave of absence, how long may it last, and what is required to return?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval; approval is not automatic. To return, the student submits a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes.

contexts.text: A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval. Employment, travel, family responsibilities, and health circumstances may support a request, but approval is not automatic.
To return from approved leave, a student submits a return notice at least 20 calendar days before regular registration closes.

qa_pairs.question: A student discussed a late add with the instructor in July 2026 but submitted the late-add request on August 5, 2026. Which registration policy version applies, and what fee is charged?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July, because the policy in force on the triggering event date controls and for registration that date is the registration action date. The student therefore pays USD 40 per course and may add only through the census date, rather than the USD 25 and seven-calendar-day window allowed by version 1.0.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.

The policy in force on the triggering event date controls unless a newer policy explicitly states that it applies retroactively. A newer publication does not silently rewrite an earlier transaction. When the event spans multiple dates, use the date identified by the policy: for registration it is the registration action date

qa_pairs.question: A student is granted an approved medical withdrawal after the census date. What tuition outcome applies, how soon must a retroactive medical request be filed, and how do scholarships affect any refund?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal, but an approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated, so a refund estimate shown before scholarship adjustment is not final.

qa_pairs.question: A student completed 60% of the assessed work before a documented emergency and asks for an `I` incomplete. Can it be granted, and what deadline would apply if one were granted?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. An `I` incomplete requires at least 70% of assessed work to be complete, so 60% does not meet the threshold, and the remaining conditions cannot compensate for it. When an incomplete is granted, the student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan, the default deadline is the end of the next regular term, and if no grade is submitted by that deadline the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.

qa_pairs.question: A student has finished every academic requirement but has an unpaid balance and a pending grade appeal in a course that affects a degree requirement. Can the degree be conferred, and does walking at commencement change that?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. Degree conferral requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. The financial hold does not erase the completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until the balance is resolved, and a financial hold also blocks graduation clearance. The pending grade appeal may separately delay conferral because the disputed course affects a degree requirement. Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred, so attending does not confer the degree.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`. A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.
Participation in a commencement ceremony is ceremonial and is not proof that a degree has been conferred.
The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.
